deep.reconstruction:
This page is a Latin draft of what became Disquisitiones Arithmeticae, art. 27, on solving a linear congruence. The printed text uses ax+t ≡ u (mod m) and square brackets [α,β,...]. Here the draft writes ax+b ≡ c, uses round brackets, and denotes the modulus also by b.

(1) Problem. Solve ax+b ≡ c (mod m) with gcd(a,m)=1.

(2) Reduction. First solve ax ≡ ±1. If x ≡ r satisfies it, i.e. ar ≡ ±1, then x ≡ ±r(c−b) (same sign) solves the original. My check: a·(±r)(c−b) = (±1)(±1)(c−b) = c−b.

(3) Diophantine form. The congruence ax ≡ ±1 (mod b) is equivalent to the indeterminate equation ax = by ± 1. Gauss remarks that its solution is 'satis nota' (well enough known from elsewhere) at this time, so he will only transcribe the algorithm.

(4) Definition of the bracket. Given a sequence α, β, γ, ..., λ, μ, form A, B, C, ..., K, L, M by:
- A = α
- B = βA + 1
- C = γB + A
- and so on, up to M = μL + K.

The symbol (α,β,γ,...,λ,μ) denotes the last term M. This is exactly the continuant. In modern terms, (α,β,...,μ) is the numerator of the continued fraction α + 1/(β + 1/(γ + ...)); for example (α,β) = αβ+1.

(5) First identity (expansion from the front): (α,β,γ,...) = α(β,γ,...) + (γ,δ,...). The recursion defines the bracket by expansion from the back. Expansion from the front follows from it together with the reversal symmetry (α,...,μ) = (μ,...,α), which the printed art. 27 states.

(6) Second identity, written with an empty right-hand side: (α,β)(β,γ) − (α,β,γ)(β). Filling it in (mine): (αβ+1)(βγ+1) − β(αβγ+α+γ) = 1. This is the first case of the determinant identity (α,...,μ)(β,...,λ) − (α,...,λ)(β,...,μ) = ±1. That identity is what makes the convergents give a solution of ax − by = ±1.

(7) Third identity, left incomplete: (1,2,3...p) = (1.2.3..6)( ) + (1.2.3..5)( ). Here 1, 2, 3, ... are index labels for the entries α1, α2, .... The evident completion (mine) is the splitting formula K(1..p) = K(1..6)·K(7..p) + K(1..5)·K(8..p), i.e. in general K(a1..ap) = K(a1..ak)K(a_{k+1}..ap) + K(a1..a_{k−1})K(a_{k+2}..ap).

Purpose. The solution of ax = by ± 1 follows from the continued-fraction quotients of a/b: with a/b = [α;β,...,μ], one has a = (α,...,μ) and b = (β,...,μ). Then x = (β,...,λ) and y = (α,...,λ) satisfy the equation by (6).
errors: Notational clash: the letter b is used both for the additive constant in ax+b ≡ c and for the modulus ('Mod. b', ax = by ± 1). The printed DA avoids this by writing ax+t ≡ u (mod m) for the congruence and ax = by ± 1 for the equation.
The identity (α,β)(β,γ) − (α,β,γ)(β) = ... is left without a right-hand side. The correct value is +1.
The splitting formula (1,2,3...p) = (1..6)( ) + (1..5)( ) is left incomplete. The correct blanks are (7,8,...,p) and (8,...,p).
The expansion (α,β,γ,...) = α(β,γ,...) + (γ,δ,...) is correct, but on the page it rests on the unstated symmetry of the bracket, since the definition recurses from the end.

results.what: Reduction of ax+b ≡ c (mod m), gcd(a,m)=1, to ax ≡ ±1, giving x ≡ ±r(c−b)
results.modern_name: solution of linear congruences via a modular inverse
results.usually_credited_to: Euler, Lagrange (18th c.); systematized in Gauss's DA art. 27 (1801)

results.what: Bracket symbol (α,β,...,μ) defined by A=α, B=βA+1, M=μL+K
results.usually_credited_to: Euler, 'Specimen algorithmi singularis' (1764); the name 'continuant' is due to Sylvester

results.what: (α,β,γ,...) = α(β,γ,...) + (γ,δ,...), together with the implicit reversal symmetry
results.modern_name: front recurrence / reversal symmetry of continuants

results.what: (α,β)(β,γ) − (α,β,γ)(β) = 1, first case of the determinant identity
results.usually_credited_to: Euler / Lagrange; printed in Gauss DA art. 27

results.what: Splitting K(1..p) = K(1..k)K(k+1..p) + K(1..k−1)K(k+2..p), here with k=6

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of DA art. 27, published 1801, using Euler's continuant algorithm. Mildly interesting points are the draft notation (round brackets, b as modulus) and the explicit splitting formula, which is not stressed in the print. Nothing here is new relative to Gauss's published work or Euler.

def K(s):
    A,B=1,0
    for t in s: A,B=t*A+B,A
    return A
a,b,c,d,e=symbols('a b c d e'); expand(K([a,b,c,d,e]) - (a*K([b,c,d,e])+K([c,d,e]))) == 0
checkable.asserts: Front expansion (α,β,γ,...) = α(β,γ,...) + (γ,δ,...), with K the continuant defined by the page's recursion
Splitting (1..9) = (1..6)(7..9) + (1..5)(8..9), the completion of the unfinished line
General determinant identity (α..μ)(β..λ) − (α..λ)(β..μ) = ±1 (here (−1)^n with n=6 entries)

transcription_corrections: Line 3: the line-end word is 'resolutionem', cramped at the margin.
The cancelled matter after 'ax' on the 'Mod. b' line looks like 'ax ≡ r(c±)1' partly overwritten. The intended reading is 'ax ≡ ±1 (Mod. b)'.
The pencil numbers '(19)' at top right and '20' in the right margin are folio/page numberings, not part of the text.
In '(α,β).(β,γ) − (α,β,γ)(β) =' the right-hand side is blank in the manuscript.
